arxiv-2001-07359.title: From far-field to near-field micro- and nanoparticle optical trapping
arxiv-2001-07359.creator: Theodoros D. Bouloumis, Síle Nic Chormaic
arxiv-2001-07359.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Theodoros D. Bouloumis, Síle Nic Chormaic. Optical tweezers is a very well-established technique that has developed into a standard tool for trapping and manipulating micron and submicron particles with great success in the last decades. Although the nature of light enforces restrictions on the minimum particle size that can be efficiently trapped due to Abbe’s diffraction limit, scientists have managed to overcome this problem by engineering new devices that exploit near-field effects.

arxiv-2406-03244.title: Electromagnetic (high-frequency) gravitational wave detectors: Interferometers revisited
arxiv-2406-03244.creator: Valerie Domcke, Joachim Kopp
arxiv-2406-03244.description: Abstract Increased interest in pushing the frontier of gravitational wave searches to higher frequencies (kHz and beyond) has resulted in a variety of different proposed experimental concepts. A significant fraction of them are based on the coupling between classical electromagnetism and gravity. We highlight some differences and similarities between different approaches, showcasing the rich phenomenology arising from this coupling.

arxiv-2410-18182.title: Precise Measurements of the LMC Bar’s Geometry With Gaia DR3 and a Novel Solution to Crowding Induced Incompleteness in Star Counting Facilities: Gaia, Astro Data Lab, UArizona HPC
arxiv-2410-18182.creator: Himansh Rathore, Yumi Choi, Knut A.G. Olsen, Gurtina Besla
arxiv-2410-18182.description: Abstract We present new measurements of the two-dimensional (2-D) geometry of the LMC’s stellar bar with precise astrometric observations of red clump stars in Gaia DR3. We develop a novel solution to tackle crowding induced incompleteness in Gaia datasets with the Gaia BP-RP color excess. Utilizing the color excess information, we derive a 2-D completeness map of the LMC’s disk.

arxiv-2411-02997.title: PV-faultNet: Optimized CNN Architecture to detect defects resulting efficient PV production

arxiv-2411-02997.description: Abstract The global shift towards renewable energy has pushed PV cell manufacturing as a pivotal point as they are the fundamental building block of green energy. However, the manufacturing process is complex enough to lose its purpose due to probable defects experienced during the time impacting the overall efficiency.

arxiv-2503-04285.description: Abstract . We introduce the space SBV X of special functions with bounded X X -variation in Carnot-Carathéodory spaces and study its main properties. Our main outcome is an approximation result, with respect to the BV X topology, for SBV X functions. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification 26B30, 53C17, 49Q15. 1.

arxiv-2505-15689.title: Weighted Lagrange Multiplier Method for Robust Source-Independent Waveform Inversion Thanks: Submitted to the editors DATE
arxiv-2505-15689.creator: Ali Gholami, Kamal Aghazade, Akshay Vishwakarma
arxiv-2505-15689.description: Abstract The Lagrange multiplier method has proven highly effective for mitigating the ill-conditioning of full waveform inversion (FWI), enabling robust and computationally efficient algorithms that converge to accurate velocity models even from poor initial estimates. Classical multiplier-based FWI methods optimize an augmented Lagrangian (AL) functional with a scalar penalty parameter that uniformly weights wave-equation constraint violations.

arxiv-2512-17777.title: Irreversible thermalization vs reversible dynamics mediated by anomalous correlators: Wave turbulence theory and experiments in optical fibers
arxiv-2512-17777.creator: T. Torres 1 , J. Garnier 2 , L. Zanaglia 3 , M. Ferraro 1,4 , C. Michel 3 , V. Doya 3 , J. Fatome 1 , B. Kibler 1 , S. Wabnitz 5 , A. Picozzi 1 , G. Millot 1
arxiv-2512-17777.description: Abstract We theoretically and experimentally investigate spontaneous self-organization in a conservative (Hamiltonian) turbulent wave system, operating far from thermodynamic equilibrium. Our system is governed by two coherently coupled nonlinear Schrödinger equations, describing the polarization evolution of light in a dispersive nonlinear optical fiber. The analysis reveals the emergence of two fundamentally distinct turbulent regimes.

pmc-10604285.title: Lived Experiences of Everyday Memory in Adults with Dyslexia: A Thematic Analysis
pmc-10604285.creator: James Hugo Smith-Spark, Elisa G. Lewis
pmc-10604285.description: Dyslexia-related difficulties with memory are well documented under laboratory conditions and via self-report questionnaires. However, the voice of the individual with dyslexia regarding the lived experience of memory across different memory systems and different daily settings is currently lacking. To address this gap in the literature, semi-structured in-depth interviews were conducted with 12 adult female university students with dyslexia.

pmc-10648858.title: Vehicle State Joint Estimation Based on Lateral Stiffness
pmc-10648858.creator: Lingxiao Quan, Ronglei Chang, Changhong Guo, Bin Li, Felipe Jiménez
pmc-10648858.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). In this study, a vehicle state joint estimation method based on lateral stiffness was applied to estimate the running states of electric vehicles driven by rear-drive, in-wheel motors. Different from the estimation methods used in other research, the joint estimator designed in this study uses the least-squares (LS) algorithm to estimate the lateral stiffness of the front and rear axles of the vehicle, deploying the high-degree cubature Kalman filter algorithm to estimate the vehicle state.

pmc-11287511.title: Sclerosing epithelioid fibrosarcoma of the pancreas: A case report
pmc-11287511.creator: Meng-Qing Sun, Li-Na Guo, Yan You, Yan-Yu Qiu, Xiao-Dong He, Xian-Lin Han
pmc-11287511.description: BACKGROUNDA sclerosing epithelioid fibrosarcoma (SEF) is a rare malignant fibroblastic soft tissue tumor that rarely occurs in intra-abdominal organs. A case of a SEF in the pancreatic head is reported herein, including its clinical manifestations, preoperative imaging features, gross specimen and pathological findings.

pmc-12641208.title: A Review of Newborn Screening Programs for Cystic Fibrosis: Are Current Protocols Appropriate for Canada's Diverse Population?
pmc-12641208.creator: Stephanie Y Cheng, Berke Sahin, Noma Abdulrahem, Paul D W Eckford, Zofia Zysman‐Colman, Mark Chilvers, Anne L Stephenson, Jocelyn Arpin, Christine Donnelly, Karen Doyle, Sara Fernandez, Corey Filiaggi, Zaiping Liu, Angela Nowak, Mary Jane Smith, Sanja Stanojevic
pmc-12641208.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundEarly diagnosis of cystic fibrosis (CF) through newborn screening (NBS) programs has improved health outcomes in people with CF (pwCF). NBS programs can vary in specific protocols and genetic variants tested, which may not perform equitably for all infants.

pmc-12711206.title: Mosquito-disseminated diflubenzuron and spinosad as alternatives to mosquito-disseminated pyriproxyfen: a proof-of-concept, blind, controlled comparison in experimental cages
pmc-12711206.creator: Gabriela Brandina Aquino de Abreu, Ayrton Sena Gouveia, Francisco Augusto da Silva Ferreira, José Joaquín Carvajal-Cortés, Cláudia Torres Codeço, Fernando Abad-Franch, Sérgio Luiz Bessa Luz, Fernando Abad-Franch
pmc-12711206.description: BACKGROUND Mosquito-disseminated pyriproxyfen (MD-PPF) is a promising novel tool for urban-mosquito control, yet resistance to PPF (a juvenile-hormone analogue) may arise in exposed mosquito populations. Alternative larvicide/pupicide molecules suitable for mosquito-driven dissemination, but with distinct modes of action, are therefore needed.

pmc-13348582.title: First-time use of deer antler-derived xenografts for management of severe peri-implantitis with titanium mesh: a case report
pmc-13348582.creator: Mahdi Kadkhodazadeh, Aida Kheiri
pmc-13348582.description: BackgroundIncreasing dental implant use correlates with rising biological complications. For severe peri-implantitis with significant bone loss, choosing the right sustaining treatment is challenging, as nonsurgical methods often fail. This case details a novel management approach for a male patient with serious peri-implantitis, specifically highlighting the initial use of deer antler xenografts in such a procedure.

pmc-13393595.title: Can hepatology lead the way? Synthesising current global curricula and proposing a model for an international specialty curriculum
pmc-13393595.creator: James C Liu Yin, Matthew Parsons, Morro ML Touray, James O’Beirne, Ponsiano Ocama, Osman Dar, Ajay Duseja, Sanjaya Satapathy, Thomas Schiano, Aftab Ala
pmc-13393595.description: BackgroundIncreased understanding and treatments for liver disease have led in recent decades to the emergence of hepatology as a subspecialty within gastroenterology, and as a standalone medical specialty. Growing challenges in hepatology are a global problem, yet no global framework for education and training has been established.
